ended: Lost the West Finals 3-4 to SA

archetype.name: Contender That Fell Short (defense-first)
archetype.definition: The defending champion ran the league's best defense and best net rating to 64 wins and two playoff sweeps, then lost the last two games of a seven-game West Finals to San Antonio.

report.headline: The league's best defense won 64, then ran out of answers against San Antonio.

recap.finish: 64-18, first in the Northwest; swept PHX and LAL, lost the West Finals 3-4 to SA
recap.body:
This was a title defense built on the other end of the floor. Oklahoma City finished first in Net Rtg at 11.2 and first in defensive rating at 107.7, about eight points per 100 possessions better than the league. That defense won in two ways. It forced turnovers (Opp TOV % 14.6, 2nd) and contested shots inside the arc well enough to hold opponents to a 51.9 Opp eFG %, 2nd. On offense it barely gave the ball away (TOV % 11.2, best in the league). The offense itself was good rather than great: 7th in rating, a step down from 3rd in each of the previous two seasons.

The season started at full speed. A 6-0 October and a 14-1 November had the Thunder at 20-1. The middle of the winter was ordinary by their standards: 9-4 in December, 9-6 in January, 8-4 in February, with scoring dropping from 123.2 a game in November to around 116. March brought them back, at 14-1 with 105.27 allowed a game, and the 16-game winning streak showed what they looked like at their best. The record was honest. W vs Pt Diff was -1 and the margin implied 65 wins, so nothing here was borrowed from close games. The one warning sign came at the very end: blowout losses at Denver and against Phoenix closed the regular season.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander carried the team and won MVP and Clutch Player of the Year. He scored 2,117 points on 66.5 TS % with a BPM of 11.7, 15.2 Win Shares and a +12.3 On-Off. Chet Holmgren was the second pillar: All-NBA Third Team and All-Defensive First Team, with 65.3 TS % and a +10.9 On-Off. Together they explain the A+ backcourt and A frontcourt grades. The depth behind them mattered too. Ajay Mitchell (+6.5 On-Off), Cason Wallace (All-Defensive Second Team) and Isaiah Joe (181 threes on 65.7 TS %) all held up. The weak spot was the wing. The group graded D, and Luguentz Dort, its only regular, posted 52.4 TS %, a -2 BPM and a -4.2 On-Off. The other two listed wings played four games each.

The late-season stumble didn't carry into April. The Thunder beat Phoenix by 35 in the opener and swept the Suns, then swept the Lakers with only the closing 115-110 win in Game 4 decided by fewer than 13. San Antonio was a different problem. Game 1 was lost in overtime at home, and wins in Games 2 and 3 gave Oklahoma City the series lead. Then the offense went cold. They scored 82 in a 21-point Game 4 loss, won Game 5, lost Game 6 91-118, and lost Game 7 at home 103-111.

The playoff numbers show where it slipped. Gilgeous-Alexander's TS % fell to 59.1 and his postseason On-Off was -18.7. Dort shot 48.9 TS % with a -14.4 On-Off, so the wing hole was exposed again on the biggest stage. Alex Caruso (+20.7) and Mitchell (+27.5) were the lineups that worked. The defensive glass also loosened, with DRB % at 71.1, 12th of 16 playoff teams.

highlights.title: A league-best, turnover-driven defense
highlights.body: The Thunder allowed the fewest points per possession in the league for a second straight year. They paired the 2nd-best Opp eFG % with the 2nd-best Opp TOV %. It is a scheme-and-personnel identity rather than a one-year spike: last season's defense also ranked 1st at 107.5, so this should travel.

highlights.title: An MVP season from Gilgeous-Alexander
highlights.body: He scored 2,117 points on 66.5 TS % with an 11.7 BPM and 15.2 Win Shares. That combination of volume and efficiency is what kept an offense with an ordinary supporting cast 7th in the league. His +12.3 On-Off shows how much the team leaned on him.

highlights.title: A record earned by margin
highlights.body: A +11.15 differential per game, 1st in the league, implied 65 wins, and they won 64. With W vs Pt Diff at -1, there is no close-game luck to regress. The baseline is real.

lowlights.title: A D-graded wing spot
lowlights.body: The wing grade was a D. Dort was its only regular and finished at -2 BPM and 52.4 TS %. In the playoffs his TS % fell to 48.9 with a -14.4 On-Off. That made him a lineup the Thunder lost minutes with, and it is the clearest roster gap the numbers show.

lowlights.title: Offense stalled late in the West Finals
lowlights.body: After taking the series lead, Oklahoma City scored 82 in Game 4 and 91 in Game 6, then lost Game 7 at home. Gilgeous-Alexander's playoff TS % dropped to 59.1, and nobody else created enough to cover for it.

lowlights.title: Few second chances, softer threes allowed
lowlights.body: An ORB % of 22.3 ranked 28th, so the offense rarely got extra possessions. Opponents also hit 36.9% from three, 25th in the league and up from 34.2% last year. The three-point defense is probably partly variance, given how well the defense contested everything else. The offensive rebounding has been low in most recent seasons and looks structural.

arc.note: A 20-1 start, a winter that was merely good, and a 14-1 March were followed by eight straight playoff wins. The season then came apart over the last four games against San Antonio.

recap.nextYear:
The core that carries forward is the same one that produced 68 and 64 wins in back-to-back years. Gilgeous-Alexander and Holmgren anchor an A+ backcourt and an A frontcourt, and the defense has now ranked 1st in rating two years running. Nothing in the record was luck: the margin implied 65 wins. If anything, the 36.9% opponents shot from three looks likelier to come down than go up. The work is on the wing, where the D grade and Dort's playoff numbers show a weak spot that a good opponent exploited. It is also on an offense that slipped from 3rd to 7th and leaned too heavily on one creator when it mattered. Hartenstein's 47 games and Mitchell's 57 are worth watching, since both posted strong On-Off numbers when available.

This was the defending champion at full strength, minus a title.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus 15 playoff games; postseason On-Off figures are small-sample.
